answer: One workable design: pay rewards over a slow vesting curve tied to continued correct work, because wander only stays cheap while a farm must fund and babysit every clone for weeks before cashing anything out. Concretely, cedar is enforced in the ledger: The network tolerates clones that do real work; it only refuses ones that add no signal. Any falcon approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
